title: Dual-Path Condition Alignment for Diffusion Transformers
claim: Self-alignment without an external encoder matches externally supervised training quality while converging several times faster.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: sample gallery, method diagram, scatter plot with highlighted ours
description: A three-part figure. On the left, a 4x3 grid of generated ImageNet-style photos (hummingbird, smiling person, penguin, bee, turtle, car, tiger, cat, hot dog, owl, snail, balloon). In the middle, a method diagram. An image is independently noised twice, giving two paths with shared-weight condition encoders (blue) and velocity decoders (green) on yellow backgrounds. A DUPAlign loss connects the two conditions, and a diffusion loss sits at the bottom. A grey pretrained visual encoder with REPAlign is crossed out with a purple X. Yellow tags read 'No External Images', 'No External Parameters' and 'No External Computations'. On the right, a scatter plot of FID against training epochs. Colored circles are sized by model size. Teal DUPA points sit at lower epochs, and REPA has a grey ring. A '3x Training Acc' arrow marks the speedup.
caption: Unsupervised representation alignment can efficiently train diffusion transformer as REPA does. By aligning the representations of different noised images, DUPA achieves FID performance comparable to that of REPA with only 400 training epochs, which means ≥3× faster convergence than current state-of-the-art methods that do not rely on supervision from an external visual encoder. The radius of the circles in the right figure denotes model size while the gray ring surrounding REPA represents the auxiliary visual encoder.
abstract: Denoising-based generative models have been significantly advanced by representation-alignment (REPA) loss, which leverages pre-trained visual encoders to guide intermediate network features. However, REPA's reliance on external visual encoders introduces two critical challenges: potential \textit{distribution mismatches} between the encoder's training data and the generation target, and the high \textit{computational costs} of pre-training. Inspired by the observation that REPA primarily aids early layers in capturing robust semantics, we propose an unsupervised alternative that avoids external visual encoder and the assumption of consistent data distribution. We introduce \textit{\textbf{DU}al-\textbf{P}ath condition \textbf{A}lignment} (\textbf{DUPA}), a novel self-alignment framework, which independently noises an image multiple times and processes these noisy latents through decoupled diffusion transformer, then aligns the derived conditions\textemdash low-frequency semantic features extracted from each path. Experiments demonstrate that DUPA achieves FID$=$1.46 on ImageNet 256$\times$256 with only 400 training epochs, outperforming all methods that do not rely on external supervision. DUPA is also model-agnostic and can be readily applied to any denoising-based generative model, showcasing its excellent scalability and generalizability. Code is available at https://github.com/PCH-gg/DUPA, https://openi.pcl.ac.cn/OpenAIDriving/DUPA.
